gate_review.Xiang_crossing: PASS_PARTIAL; ferry/pontoon capacity adequate for staged continuation, not unrestricted mass movement
gate_review.air_support: PASS_TACTICAL; fighter/recon servicing advanced, heavy sustained bomber-basing still limited
gate_review.Fourteenth_AF_effect: Continues to impose bridge/rail repair delays and supply loss, but no multi-day ammunition/POL starvation at the campaign level
gate_review.Chinese_force_density: Hengyang-Leiyang defense remains substantial; no assumption that Changsha withdrawal implies collapse

decision: PHASE_B_GO_PREPARATION_23_MAY; movement/recon concentration begins 24 May; no instant Hengyang assault
why_go: Hengyang is a major rail/air/command node whose capture compounds the node-transfer strategy rather than merely extending the map front
Changsha-Xiangtan has crossed the minimum operational-transfer threshold needed to support another bound
Japanese field-army cohesion and stocks remain adequate
Chinese field army is preserved, so delay also allows it to deepen defenses; indefinite consolidation is not cost-free
why_not_immediate_assault: Hengyang defense is denser and more prepared than the Changsha rear-guard system
forward airfield and bridge throughput are still partial
Japanese objective is node capture at acceptable cost, not momentum for its own sake
